styles.name: speedometer
styles.description: Classic 270° arc speedometer: tick marks at every 10%, a redline zone above 80%, and a line needle pointing to the eased progress value

styles.name: ring-progress
styles.description: Thin full-circle ring that fills clockwise from 12 o'clock; the filled arc length = eased × 2π, the unfilled portion stays dim

styles.name: half-gauge
styles.description: 180° semicircle gauge (fuel/temperature style): arc spans left→right across the top of the cell, a needle swings from empty (left) to full (right)

styles.name: tachometer
styles.description: Tachometer: 270° rev-counter dial with a needle that overshoots the target and damps back — the settle wobble is driven by ctx.time so the needle visibly hunts to the eased value

styles.name: donut
styles.description: Thick donut / pie: a filled wedge between an inner and outer radius sweeps clockwise from 12 o'clock as eased grows — the hole stays empty, the wedge fills with braille dots

styles.name: signal-arc
styles.description: Concentric arc bands like a cell-signal or Wi-Fi icon: each tier is a thicker arc; bands light up from innermost outward as eased rises

styles.name: compass
styles.description: Compass rose: a full circle with N/E/S/W tick marks and a bearing needle that points to eased × 360° — progress literally steers the heading

styles.name: vu-needle
styles.description: Analog VU-meter needle: the needle bounces rhythmically around the eased level driven by ctx.time, mimicking the momentum of a real moving-coil meter in a recording studio

styles.name: segmented-ring
styles.description: Discrete LED-style segments arranged around a full ring: each is a short arc of dots separated by a small gap; segments light up clockwise from 12 o'clock one by one as eased rises

styles.name: dual-gauge
styles.description: Two concentric arc gauges: the outer ring tracks eased progress while the inner ring oscillates with time, showing a secondary live reading (e.g. instantaneous vs. average) in the same braille dial

styles.name: clock-face
styles.description: Analog clock face: progress maps the full 12-hour cycle — hour hand completes one revolution at 100%, minute hand moves 12× faster, giving a two-hand clock whose time equals eased × 12:00

styles.name: pressure-dial
styles.description: Pressure gauge with a hatched danger arc beyond 75% and a needle that overdamps into place — slow creep at low pressure, urgent quiver at high; danger zone fills with a dense dot pattern when eased exceeds the threshold

styles.name: altimeter
styles.description: Aviation altimeter: ten rim ticks like the 0–9 altitude scale, a long needle spinning 10 revolutions over the full range (hundreds) and a short needle making a single revolution (thousands)

styles.name: radar-scope
styles.description: Radar scope: concentric range rings with a sweep beam rotating on ctx.time; contact blips at pseudo-random bearings appear one by one as eased rises — at 100% the screen is full of traffic

styles.name: attitude-horizon
styles.description: Artificial horizon (attitude indicator): the horizon line climbs the bezel as eased rises — ground hatching shrinks away below — while a gentle time-driven roll banks the whole horizon; fixed wings mark centre

styles.name: bubble-level
styles.description: Spirit level spanning the full width: a gently curved vial with centre marks; the bubble starts at the far end and drifts toward dead centre as eased approaches 1 — level achieved at 100%

styles.name: edgewise-meter
styles.description: Edgewise panel meter spanning the full width: a horizontal scale with ticks every 10% and a hatched red zone past 85%; a slanted needle pivots from below the panel to the eased position, like rack-mount audio gear

styles.name: dial-bank
styles.description: A bank of three mini speedometers side by side: progress cascades — the first dial sweeps 0–33%, the second 33–66%, the third 66–100% — like a rack of instruments coming alive one by one

styles.name: galvanometer
styles.description: Laboratory galvanometer: the needle hangs from a pivot at the TOP of the instrument and swings across an arc scale at the bottom — the inverted geometry of a mirror galvanometer, with a slow critically-damped settle toward the eased deflection

styles.name: anemometer
styles.description: Anemometer: a three-cup wind rotor whose spin rate tracks eased — barely turning at 0%, a blur at 100% — ringed by a dotted bearing race; the cups are small circles at the arm tips
